insight.title: Why You Still Find Problems When Life Gets Better
insight.subtitle: Why solving a big issue makes you focus on a smaller one

sections.text:
Ever wonder why life’s irritations never seem to disappear? Research shows that as big problems vanish, your brain naturally lowers its threshold for what qualifies as a "problem" to keep the workload constant.
This is prevalence-induced concept change. Your mind has a fixed quota for trouble. When real threats decrease, your internal radar recalibrates, labeling minor inconveniences as major issues simply to fill the empty space.
It’s why a slow app feels as stressful today as a missed deadline did years ago. You aren’t surrounded by more problems; your brain is just expanding its definition of what counts as "bad."
The next time you feel annoyed by a small inconvenience today, ask if your standards just shifted.
You aren't losing your peace; you're just hunting for a reason to be alert.

news.description: New Delhi [India], April 7: The All-India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), in collaboration with the Gut Microbiota and Probiotic Science Foundation (India), hosted the 16th India Probiotic Symposium on March 27-28, 2026 at the Jawaharlal Nehru Auditorium, AIIMS, New Delhi.
